newsitem.title: BULGARIA: NO RATE CUT THIS MONTH - BULGARIAN C.BANK GOVERNOR.
newsitem.headline: NO RATE CUT THIS MONTH - BULGARIAN C.BANK GOVERNOR.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) does not plan to reduce its record high central interest rate of 300 percent until the monetary system shows signs of improvement, BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Tuesday.

"We will not cut the rate until we have seen some positive signs from the monetary system and until the International Monetary Fund mission arrives to review the reform performance," Filipov told reporters.
An IMF mission is expected in Sofia to complete its reform programme review by the end of this month or beginning of November.
The BNB hiked the rate to an all-time high last month in a bid to stabilise the crumbling financial system, saying the measure was temporary.

The extra burden of the high interest on the budget will be offset by revenue from sell-offs of big state enterprises, said Filipov. The government recently announced plans to sell off some 20 big state firms.

Speaking after a meeting with deputies from the ruling Socialist party, largely composed of ex-communists, Filipov said that none of nine banks placed under special supervision will be taken off the list.

The BNB placed nine state and private banks under special supervision last month due to blocked settlements and inadequately law capital to risk assets ratios. The BNB appointed sequestrators at the nine banks, who were due to evaluate their financial state.
Under Bulgaria banking law the BNB can hold a bank under special supervision for a maximum of one year.

The IMF delayed a crucial $115 million tranche until the government sped up privatisation, effectively closed down 64 lossmakers and stabilised its shaky banking sector. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
